subject: ventures/changepoint-detector
professional: a statistician who does changepoint and structural-break analysis (would check first: is PELT exact under the stated cost and penalty, does BOCPD match Adams & MacKay, are the known literature changepoints reproduced, and does the default overcut autocorrelated real series)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with code written by the auditor (scratchpad chk/indep.py, c1.py, c2.py, c3.py), not the venture's: (1) Nile mean model, plain optimal partitioning with sd = MAD(diff)/(0.6745 sqrt 2) and penalty 2 ln n: changepoint [28] (1899), cost 129.332896, sd 115.319389; engine pelt identical to 6 digits; Cobb (1978) also puts the change after 1898. (2) Nile meanvar, Gaussian cost, 3 ln n, min segment 10: [28], cost 1265.2911 both. (3) Coal-mining disasters Poisson: own DP gives [41, 97] = 1892 and 1948, cost 115.9927, engine identical; the 1891/1892 break agrees with Raftery & Akman (1986). (4) ruptures 1.1.10 Pelt (pip-installed here, l2 with pen = beta*sd^2, normal cost with pen = 3 ln n etc.) on 120 FRESH seeded series (seed 20261119, 60-240 points, 0-3 changes, mean and meanvar, bic/aic/hq): 120 of 120 identical changepoints. (5) Own Adams & MacKay BOCPD (NIG, Student-t predictive via scipy.stats.t, hazard 1/100, engine's prior): P(change at 1899) 0.786189 both, max abs difference over all 100 points 1.04e-11, log evidence -640.47652 both. Kept at 3 not 4: the add-on models (trend, drift, synthetic control, watch) were not recomputed, and an --ar1 replicate on fresh seeds came out at 8/40 false alarms against the README's 4/40.
evidence.completeness: Checked end to end: CLI --example (Nile, agreed panel, segments, ranges, Bayesian detections; 0.19 s), CLI on a quoted-thousands CSV with blank and n/a rows (2 skipped, change found), constant series (no change), too-short input and unknown column (plain errors), 100,001 points rejected with a message, served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin left), agreed-change F1 figures traced to eval/tcpd-heldout.out.txt. Did not exercise the browser page interactively, the Stripe fetcher (needs a key), or the webhook path.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture: 979 tests, 979 pass, 0 fail, 9 min 16 s (555.8 s). Mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py against a fast core subset of engine.test.mjs (33 tests, 2.5 s): robustSd sqrt2 dropped caught; BOCPD lag off-by-one caught; PELT prune bound vi - beta -> vi + beta caught; meanvar penalty k 3 -> 2 caught; BIC constant k ln n -> (k+0.5) ln n SURVIVED the core subset (ruptures and brute-force tests pass because both sides share penaltyValue or use numeric penalties) and was caught only by the full engine.test.mjs (64.5 s). A first prune mutant (vi - 2 beta) was equivalent (less pruning stays exact) and is not counted.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (pelt, peltMeanLoop, makeCost, penaltyValue, robustSd, bocpd, parseSeries, nigLogMarginal), consensus.mjs, cli.mjs output. The core is careful (prefix sums, typed arrays, pruning documented with perf notes in docs/history) but engine.mjs has grown from 2243 lines (2026-11-09 audit) to 3004, README.md is 7951 lines with 229 headings, 217 test files sit in the venture root with no runner config, and the suite takes over 9 minutes. parseSeries returns column: undefined when the header is narrower than the rows (engine.mjs:1060).
evidence.claims: Backed: Nile 1899 / means 1097.75 and 849.97 / 79% (reproduced: 78.6%); ruptures 100/100 (I re-ran a fresh 120/120); Poisson brute force; agreed-panel F1 0.71/0.30/0.64 matches eval/tcpd-heldout.out.txt lines 7, 25, 11; limits section is frank (shape changes, causes, 100,000 points). Disclaimer and local-only usage counts in README and index.html (usage.mjs import at index.html:267). Stale: README.md:76 says 581 tests (now 979). Partial: --ar1 null false alarms 4/40 and power 35/40 (README.md:125-127) came out 8/40 and 32/40 on my seeds; stated from one seed set with no interval. The agreed-panel sentence omits that binseg scored 0.727 on the same held-out set (higher than the panel).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an analyst pastes a daily CSV with thousands separators and gaps and asks whether and when it shifted; the CLI gives the date, the size in noise sds, a 95% range and a Bayesian probability, leading with the changes all six settings agree on. That is a job a practitioner can finish. The held-out TCPD numbers show the single default level model scores F1 0.30, below reporting no change (0.64), so a user who reads only the level model on a real autocorrelated series gets overcut; the output leads with the agreed panel to mitigate this.
evidence.domain: Compared against Killick et al. (2012) PELT, Jackson et al. (2005) optimal partitioning, Adams & MacKay (2007) BOCPD and Murphy's NIG conjugate formulas, plus ruptures and the literature changepoints for Nile and coal: the methods match the published standard exactly. Departures are documented (MAD-of-differences sd fixed once, BIC 2 ln n / 3 ln n, priors centred on the data). A senior statistician would sign off the core with the stated limits; the default's overcutting on autocorrelated real series is the main professional caveat, disclosed.

mutations.change: case 'bic': return k * Math.log(n); -> return (k + 0.5) * Math.log(n);
case 'bic': return k * Math.log(n); -> return (k + 0.5) * Math.log(n);

defects.what: The default BIC constant (k ln n) is still not pinned (open since the 2026-11-09 audit): changing it to (k+0.5) ln n passes all 33 core tests including the ruptures cross-check, the brute-force checks and Nile, because the ruptures fixture uses numeric penalties and the brute-force reference calls the same penaltyValue. Only a slower downstream test in the full engine.test.mjs (64 s) fails. A one-line assert of penaltyValue('bic', n, model) per model, beside the existing HQ test at engine.test.mjs:810, closes it.

engine.mjs has grown from 2243 lines (2026-11-09) to 3004, mixing the algorithm core, count/trend/AR pipelines, CSV parsing and report helpers; README.md is 7951 lines with 229 headings, so the user-facing guidance is buried in a research log.
README states 581 tests (2026-11-12); the suite now has 979.

parseSeries does not check the header width against the rows: a one-column header over two-field rows (a comma-decimal single column such as 1,5) is silently read as label,value and the series name comes out as 'undefined' in the summary.
The --ar1 false-alarm and power figures (4/40, 35/40) are from one seed set without an interval; fresh seeds gave 8/40 and 32/40, so the README reads more precise than the measurement.

The full suite takes 9 min 16 s over 217 test files in the venture root with no fast-core target, so contributors are unlikely to run it whole; a 'core' script running the 33 engine tests used here (2.5 s) would catch most core regressions.

verdict: The statistical core is expert-grade: five recomputations with auditor-written code (Nile mean and meanvar optimal partitioning, coal-mining Poisson, an Adams & MacKay BOCPD agreeing to 1e-11, and ruptures 1.1.10 on 120 fresh seeds, 120/120) matched the engine exactly, and the Nile and coal breaks agree with the literature. All 979 tests pass, and 4 of 5 non-equivalent core mutants were caught by a 2.5 s core subset; the BIC constant mutant survived that subset again (the 2026-11-09 defect is still open) and was caught only by the full engine test file. Claims trace to eval files and the limits are frank, but the README's test count is stale and the --ar1 figures are single-seed. Craft is below the bar: engine.mjs grew to 3004 lines and the README to 7951. It meets the bar (correctness, claims, verification 3; median 3) and is finished; scores are as found on 2026-11-19, before any fix.
